definition: Pangram is an artificial intelligence detection software developed to identify text produced by large language models (LLMs), developed by Brooklyn-based Pangram Labs.
details: It has been used in a number of high-profile accusations of AI use in published writing, and criticized for contributing to "witch hunts" for AI writing.

explainer.lead: Pangram is artificial intelligence detection software built to identify text produced by large language models, developed by Brooklyn-based Pangram Labs. It matters because such detectors are being used in real accusations about published writing.

tiers.eli5: It is a tool that reads a piece of writing and guesses whether a computer wrote it.
tiers.practitioner: It is applied to flag suspect text, including in published writing. A pitfall is that accusations based on detector output have been criticized for contributing to 'witch hunts' for AI writing.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a commercial detection system rather than a published formal method; what is known is that it aims to identify text produced by large language models. There is no stated accuracy bound, and its use in accusations has drawn criticism.

explainer.example: A publisher runs a submitted article through Pangram, and a positive result becomes part of a public accusation that the text was AI-generated.
